title: apcore ACL Configuration Schema
description: JSON Schema for validating ACL YAML configuration files. Based on PROTOCOL_SPEC Section 6.

version.description: ACL configuration version. MAJOR.MINOR or MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. The PATCH component is optional because every documented ACL example in this repository uses the two-part form `"1.0"` (docs/features/acl-system.md, docs/guides/acl-configuration.md, examples/acl/agent-tool-governance.yaml) — a full-semver pattern rejected the repository's own shipped example. No SDK reads this field.

default_effect.description: Default effect when no rule matches a caller/target pair. MUST be 'allow' or 'deny'. Defaults to 'deny' for security.

rules.description: Ordered list of ACL rules. Rules are evaluated in DEFINITION ORDER using a first-match-wins strategy — the first rule whose caller and target patterns both match determines the decision (PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.3). They are NOT sorted by priority, and there is no deny-over-allow precedence at equal priority.

ACLRule.description: A single ACL rule that matches callers against targets and applies an effect.

id.description: RESERVED — not evaluated by any implementation. PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.3 states that `id`, `actions` and `priority` are reserved for future specification versions and SHOULD NOT be used. Retained so existing files still validate; the logging/debugging identifier has no effect on rule evaluation.

callers.description: List of caller module ID patterns. Supports wildcards: '*' matches any characters. Special values: '@external' for top-level/external calls, '@system' for internal system calls.

targets.description: List of target module ID patterns. Supports wildcards: '*' matches any characters.

actions.description: RESERVED — not evaluated by any implementation. PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.3 states that `id`, `actions` and `priority` are reserved for future specification versions and SHOULD NOT be used. Retained so existing files still validate; the action list has no effect on rule evaluation.

effect.description: The effect to apply when this rule matches. 'allow' permits the call, 'deny' rejects it.

priority.description: RESERVED — not evaluated by any implementation. PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.3 states that `id`, `actions` and `priority` are reserved for future specification versions and SHOULD NOT be used. Retained so existing files still validate; the priority ordering has no effect on rule evaluation.

description.description: Human-readable description of the rule's purpose.

RuleConditions.description: Additional conditions for rule matching (beyond caller/target patterns).

identity_types.description: Only match when the caller's identity type is one of these values.

items.description: An identity type. PROTOCOL_SPEC §5 declares this a free-form string; the well-known values are shown in examples. conformance/fixtures/acl_agent_scoping.json uses `ai`, which a closed enum rejected.

roles.description: Only match when the caller has at least one of these roles. Named `roles` per PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.3; the schema previously called this `identity_roles`, a name that appears in no document, example or fixture.

time_window.description: Only match during specific time windows.

max_call_depth.description: Only match when call chain depth does not exceed this value.

$or.description: Compound: passes if ANY sub-condition object passes; each sub-object's keys are AND-ed internally. Sub-objects MAY nest further compound operators. PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.3.

$not.description: Compound: passes if the wrapped condition object FAILS. An empty object MUST evaluate to false (fail-closed). PROTOCOL_SPEC §6.3.

enabled.description: Whether to enable ACL audit logging.

include_denied.description: Whether to log denied access attempts.
